title: A scheme unramified over a field is discrete
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be an unramified morphism [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then the underlying topological space of $Y$ is discrete: every point $y\in Y$ is open in $Y$ (so every subset of $Y$ is open, and every point of $Y$ is also closed). (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), part (1), direction "only if", topological part; Stacks proves it from Algebra, Lemma 00UW (residue fields finite separable), Morphisms, Lemma 02V5 (unramified implies locally quasi-finite) and Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (a point at which a morphism locally of finite type is quasi-finite is isolated in its fibre).)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), statement part (1) and proof, lines 7790-7826
